title: Kale (1913): Bhartṛhari's śatakas with a Sanskrit commentary
description: The scan begins with an English table of contents. Then comes the Sanskrit text of two śatakas, the Nītiśataka and the Vairāgyaśataka, each followed by its miscellaneous stanzas: each verse, in large type, is followed by its Sanskrit commentary in smaller type, some verses are introduced by a short lead-in, and numbered footnotes, mostly variant readings, sit below a rule at the foot of the page and restart at 1 on each page. After the Sanskrit text come an English translation, one numbered paragraph per stanza, and English notes on the stanzas, which quote Sanskrit words in Devanagari.

flows.main: The contents, the Sanskrit text, the translation and the notes, in reading order.

contents.description: The table of contents at the start of the scan.

section.description: One śataka of the Sanskrit text, such as वैराग्यशतकम्, with its opening, its stanzas and its miscellaneous stanzas.

translation.description: The English translation, after the Sanskrit text: one unit for the translation of both śatakas and their miscellaneous stanzas. Its headings, such as TRANSLATION, NĪTIS'ATAK., MISCELLANEOUS. and VAIRĀGYAS'ATAKA., are inside it, and it goes on across them.

notes.description: The English notes on the stanzas, after the translation: one unit for the notes on both śatakas and their miscellaneous stanzas. Its headings, such as NOTES, MISCELLANEOUS. and VAIRĀGYAS'ATAKA., are inside it, and it goes on across them.

heading.description: A title or heading: a part's title, such as CONTENTS., TRANSLATION or NOTES.; a śataka's title, such as अथ श्रीमद्भर्तृहरिविरचितं above नीतिशतकम् ।; an invocation above it, such as ॥ श्रीः ॥ or ॥ श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥; a topic heading inside a śataka, such as अथ तृष्णादूषणम् ।; or a heading for the miscellaneous stanzas.

paragraph.description: A paragraph of English prose that is neither a stanza's translation nor its note: a line of the contents, such as The S'atakas treat of the following themes:—, or an editor's note, such as N. B. Read the slokas on p. 16 in this order—91, 86, ….

contents_entry.description: One line of the table of contents: a range of stanza numbers and its theme, such as 2—14 अज्ञनिन्दा or Ignorance censured.

commentator_verse.description: One of the commentator's own opening verses at the start of the Nītiśataka, in the commentary's type, before his introduction; each ends with ॥.

introduction.description: The commentator's introduction at the start of a śataka, in the commentary's type, after his opening verses and before the first verse of Bhartṛhari.

group.description: One verse with its lead-in, if any, and its commentary. The app can show each group on its own.

lead_in.description: A short line of its own that introduces the verse.

verse.description: One verse in large type, with its number, such as ॥ २६ ॥.

commentary.description: The Sanskrit commentary on the verse, in smaller type. It usually ends with the name of the metre, such as शिखरिणी ॥.

translated_stanza.description: The English translation of one stanza: a paragraph beginning with the stanza's number, such as 4. or I.; some are only a cross-reference, such as 1 See p. 16.

stanza_note.description: The English note on one stanza, from its number, such as Sl. 5., to the next note. A note can have several paragraphs, each its own region, and can run across pages.

footnote.description: One footnote below the rule: in the Sanskrit text, a numbered variant reading; in the English parts, a note marked * or †.

running_header.description: The running title of the Sanskrit text, such as वैराग्यशतकम् ।

page_number.description: The printed page number: in Devanagari digits in the Sanskrit text, and in the English parts in brackets, such as [ 20 ], or parentheses, such as ( 43 ), at the head of the page.

relations.note: A footnote marker in the text points to its footnote.

conventions: Transcribe Devanagari as printed, in Unicode NFC, with the printed digits and dandas.
Transcribe English as printed, with the diacritics and apostrophes of transliterated Sanskrit as printed, such as S'ataka, Kâvyâdars'a and mâlatí. Italics are not marked.
